checklist.title: Passport Renewal Checklist
checklist.subtitle: Everything the Myanmar Embassy in Singapore asks for: how to get an appointment, what to bring, what it costs, and how the counter runs on the day.
checklist.scamWarningTitle: Appointments are free. Nobody can sell you one.
checklist.scamWarningBody: The embassy has said it authorised no company or agent to arrange passport renewals for a fee, and that it runs no Facebook, Instagram or TikTok account. Anyone charging you for an appointment, or claiming to be embassy staff on social media, is not the embassy.
checklist.scamReportLink: Report a paid appointment seller on the embassy WhatsApp {number}

embassyContact.title: Embassy — where and who to call
embassyContact.subtitle: Tap the address for a map, or a number to call. The consular line is for Myanmar citizens; the visa line is for visa questions only.
embassyContact.mapsHint: Tap to open the map — nearest MRT is Napier.

visa.name: Visa line
visa.hours: Visa questions only — not for passport appointments

appointment.title: Step 1 — Get an appointment on WhatsApp
appointment.subtitle: The website booking system is suspended. Appointments are arranged only through the embassy's own WhatsApp numbers, split by which pass you hold.

longTermPasses.passes: PR, Employment Pass, S Pass, Dependent Pass, Long Term Pass

steps.chooseNumber: Message the number for your own pass type. Sending to the wrong one usually means no reply.
steps.sendCopies: Send photos of your documents for checking — the passport data page, and the front and back of your pass card.
steps.onePerPhone: One appointment per phone number. To book for family from the same number, attach proof you are the same family.
steps.dontRepeat: Do not send the same request twice. Extra messages can send you back to the end of the waiting list.
steps.checkList: Watch for the approved list published on the embassy website every Friday, and find your name on it. Your date is usually about two weeks after you message.
steps.comeOnDate: Your date and time are fixed. Come on that date only — turning up on another day will not get you served.

checklist.documentsSubtitle: Two copies, not one. The embassy rejects an application outright when an original is missing, and the officer can ask for more documents than are listed here.

items.form: The application form for your own pass type, filled in and signed — 2 copies. There is a different form for PR, EP, S Pass, Student Pass, Dependent Pass / LTVP, Work Permit, domestic helper and seaman.
items.photo: One passport photo taken within the last 6 months: white background, ears visible, no glasses. Bring your own — the embassy does not take photos, though it will take another one there for the machine-readable passport.
items.passport: Your passport: the original, plus 2 copies of the data page and the observations / endorsement pages.
items.passCard: Your Work Permit, S Pass, EP, Student Pass or Dependent Pass card: the original plus 2 copies. PR holders bring the card with the Re-Entry Permit (Form 7).
items.taxReceipt: Your income tax receipt from the embassy — original and a copy, if you have one. Never paid before? Do the tax payment first (see below).
items.cash: Enough cash. The embassy takes cash only — no cards, no PayNow, no mobile payment of any kind.

checklist.situationsTitle: Extra documents, depending on who you are

situations.dependent: Applying as a dependent: household list, birth certificate or marriage certificate (original + 2 copies), plus the passport and IC of the person you depend on (originals + copies).
situations.student: Student Pass holder: your student pass (original + copy) and a recommendation letter from your school.
situations.seaman: Seaman: your CDC (original + copy) and your Basic Safety Training certificate (the 4 tickets).
situations.permanentResident: PR: the Re-Entry Permit (Form 7), and be ready to show an IRAS or company letter if asked.
situations.pjType: Holding a PJ-type passport, or changing away from one: originals and copies of your Work Permit, S Pass, EP or PR card with Re-Entry Form 7.
situations.airTicketDeposit: Myanmar woman married to a foreign national and applying as a dependent: the receipt for the S$500 return air-ticket deposit.

checklist.visitSubtitle: The counter opens in the morning for submissions and reopens in the afternoon for collection. Closed on weekends and public holidays.

visit.gettingThere: 15 St Martin's Drive, Singapore 257996. Nearest MRT: Napier (Thomson–East Coast Line). Leave extra time — the embassy is a walk from the station.
visit.submission: Submit your application in the morning: Monday to Friday, 8.30am to 12.00 noon.
visit.collection: Collect your finished passport in the afternoon: 3.00pm to 4.00pm.
visit.cashOnly: Bring cash. Cards and e-payment are not accepted for any consular service, including tax payment.
visit.noPhotoService: There is no photo service at the embassy — have your photo taken before you go.
visit.originals: Bring every original. Without them your application is rejected, and the consular officer may ask for documents beyond this list.
visit.enquiryCalls: Consular enquiry line for Myanmar citizens: +65 6735 2035, answered between 1pm and 3pm on working days.

fees.title: What it costs
fees.subtitle: Published embassy fees in Singapore dollars. These are the totals to bring, including surcharges.

items.earlyRenewal: Renewing while more than 1 year of validity remains
items.legalisation: Legalisation of one Singapore-issued document (7 working days)

fees.note: Cash only. Fees are set by the embassy and can change — check the consular page before you go, and never pay a fee to anyone other than the embassy counter.

tax.title: If you have never paid income tax at the embassy
tax.subtitle: Renewal asks for a tax receipt, so the tax payment often has to be done first. It is a separate, cash-only application at the same counter.

items.taxForm: The tax application form, downloaded from the embassy website and filled in.
items.passportCopy: A copy of your passport data page (bring the original too).
items.singaporeIcCopy: A copy of your Singapore pass card — Work Permit, S Pass, EP or PR card.
items.myanmarIcCopy: A copy of your Myanmar NRC, plus any earlier tax receipts you have.

lost.title: If your passport is lost
lost.subtitle: This is a different application, and it starts with a Singapore police report, not at the embassy.

items.policeReport: Make a Singapore police report first — online, or in person at a Neighbourhood Police Centre with your work pass — and bring the report with you.
items.twoForms: Two copies of the personal history form, and two recent white-background photos.
items.oldPassportCopies: Two copies each of the data page and the last endorsement page of the lost passport, plus your pass card (original + 2 copies).
items.householdList: Two copies of your Myanmar NRC and two copies of your household list, front and back.
items.taxReceipt: Your tax receipt, original and copy, if you have one.
items.seaman: Seaman: CDC (original + copy) and Basic Safety Training certificates (the 4 tickets).
items.airTicketDeposit: Married to a foreign national: the S$500 return air-ticket deposit receipt.
items.certificateOfIdentity: Flying home soon? A Certificate of Identity must be applied for at least one week before departure.

otherServices.title: Other consular services
otherServices.subtitle: Not a standard renewal? Each service has its own form and document list on the embassy site — download the form, then confirm the current list there before you go.

newborn.name: Newborn baby passport
newborn.hint: Forms for both parents and the baby, plus birth and marriage certificates (original + 2 sets). S Pass and EP holders also need a company sponsor letter. A second application uses a different form — get it from the consular page.

seamanToShore.name: Seaman passport to shore-job passport
seamanToShore.hint: Job assignment letter, CDC and 4 tickets, passport, Singapore stay-pass card, and tax receipts if any — 2 sets of the form.

coi.name: Certificate of Identity
coi.hint: For a newborn or a lost passport, when you need to fly soon. Apply at least one week before departure and bring the air ticket.

dependentLetter.name: Recommendation letter for being a dependent
dependentLetter.hint: Request form, your IC and passport, household list or birth/marriage certificate, and the sponsor's tax receipt.

airTicketDeposit.name: Return air-ticket deposit (S$500)
airTicketDeposit.hint: For a Myanmar woman married to a foreign national. Bring the request form, both passports and ICs.

airTicketRefund.name: Withdraw the air-ticket deposit
airTicketRefund.hint: Allowed after divorce, change of nationality, returning to Myanmar for good, the husband's death, or after 3 years. Submit 9.00am–12.00 noon.

legalisation.name: Legalisation of Singapore documents
legalisation.hint: Notarise in Singapore, then certify at the Singapore Academy of Law, then the embassy (S$50 cash per document, 7 working days). Submit 9.30am–12.00 noon at the information counter.

forms.title: Download the official forms
forms.subtitle: Print, fill in by hand, sign, and bring two copies. The embassy website is always the current source.

checklist.prepareTitle: The night before — pack this pile

prepare.formSigned: Two signed copies of the form for your own pass type.
prepare.copies: Two copies of the passport data page, observations pages, pass card (front and back) and Myanmar NRC.
prepare.photo: One recent white-background photo. The embassy will not take one for you.
prepare.cash: Enough cash for the fee. No cards, no PayNow.
prepare.originals: The original passport, pass card and any tax receipt. Missing originals mean a rejected application.
prepare.appointmentName: Check that your name is on this week's approved list, and that you are going on that date only.

checklist.officialLinksTitle: Check the embassy's own pages before you go
checklist.officialLinksSubtitle: Requirements, forms for each pass type and the weekly appointment list all live on the embassy website, and it is the only source that is always current.
checklist.sourceDisclaimer: Checked against the Myanmar Embassy Singapore's own consular page and homepage in September 2026. Requirements, fees and appointment channels change without notice — confirm on the embassy website, or on the consular enquiry line, before your appointment.
checklist.remittanceWarningTitle: Remittance rule that can affect your passport renewal
checklist.remittanceWarningBody: Since September 2023, Myanmar requires citizens working abroad to remit at least 25% of foreign wages home through an official bank or licensed remittance provider (not informal channels like hundi). Reports indicate non-compliance can affect passport renewal — keep proof of your official remittances.

steps.book: Then book a visit on the High Commission's e-appointment portal for biometrics and payment (NETS at the counter).
steps.confirm: Standard renewal is often 4–6 weeks. Collect the passport yourself, weekday afternoons — confirm hours on the mission site.

steps.start: Malaysian passports are renewed through the High Commission of Malaysia in Singapore.
steps.book: Use the High Commission's passport-renewal page for the current appointment system and document list.
steps.confirm: Fees, hours and required papers change. Confirm on that page before you take leave to go.

emergency.subtitle: Tap any number to call it. The red numbers are for danger right now; below them are the helplines for salary, health, abuse and scam problems.
emergency.missionSubtitle: For a lost passport, a death in the family, or when you need your own government's help.

work.title: Work, salary and employer problems
work.subtitle: Unpaid salary, no rest day, confiscated passport, illegal deployment, threats of repatriation.

health.title: Health and mental health
health.subtitle: Not life-threatening, but you are unwell, injured, or struggling to cope.

safety.title: Abuse, violence and scams
safety.subtitle: When someone is hurting you or trying to take your money.

police.name: Police
police.hint: A crime, violence, or someone is in immediate danger.
police.smsHint: Not safe to speak? Text 70999 — say what is happening and exactly where you are.

ambulanceFire.name: Ambulance / Fire
ambulanceFire.hint: Life-threatening injury or illness, fire, or someone trapped.
ambulanceFire.smsHint: Deaf, hard of hearing or unable to speak? SCDF's emergency SMS is 70995.

momMdw.name: MOM Helpline for Domestic Workers
momMdw.hint: For domestic workers in distress — abuse, not enough food, unpaid salary, no rest day.
momMdw.hours: Mon–Fri, 8.30am–5.30pm. From overseas: +65 6339 5505. Your call is kept confidential.

mom.name: MOM Contact Centre
mom.hint: Ministry of Manpower — work pass questions and reports about salary, housing or illegal deployment.
mom.hours: Mon–Fri, 8.30am–5.30pm, except public holidays. Outside these hours, use the online form.

mwc.name: Migrant Workers' Centre (MWC)
mwc.hint: Salary disputes, workplace injury, repatriation and recruitment debt. Free legal advice at their Law Centre.
mwc.hours: 24 hours, in about 10 migrant worker languages.

cde.name: Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE)
cde.hint: Advice and mediation for domestic workers, and temporary shelter if you cannot stay in the house.

twc2.name: Transient Workers Count Too (TWC2)
twc2.hint: Help with salary claims and injury cases, plus free meals and help finding a place to stay.

home.name: HOME — Migrant Workers
home.hint: Employment advice and legal aid for non-domestic workers cheated or exploited by an employer or agent.
home.hours: Call, SMS or WhatsApp the same number. Help desk: 720 Geylang Road, Mon–Fri, 10am–5pm.

homeMdw.name: HOME — Domestic Workers
homeMdw.hint: Shelter, food and legal help if you are abused or exploited. Burmese-speaking help desk at Peninsula Plaza on Sundays.
homeMdw.hours: Call, SMS or WhatsApp the same number.

healthserve.name: HealthServe Crisis Helpline
healthserve.hint: Free counselling and medical help for migrant workers, with staff who speak your language.
healthserve.hours: 24 hours. Also runs a low-cost clinic and dental clinic in Geylang.

sos.name: Samaritans of Singapore (SOS)
sos.hint: If you feel hopeless or are thinking of ending your life, talk to someone now. Free and confidential.
sos.hours: 24 hours. If you cannot talk, message CareText on WhatsApp instead.

nurseFirst.name: NurseFirst
nurseFirst.hint: Sick but not an emergency, and unsure where to go? A nurse tells you which clinic to use.
nurseFirst.hours: For non-emergency medical advice. Cheaper than going to a hospital A&E.

nonEmergencyAmbulance.name: Non-Emergency Ambulance
nonEmergencyAmbulance.hint: Transport to hospital when the condition is not life-threatening. A fee applies.
nonEmergencyAmbulance.hours: SCDF will close this line on 1 January 2027. Never use it for a life-threatening case — call 995.

navh.name: National Anti-Violence and Sexual Harassment Helpline
navh.hint: Family violence, sexual harassment or abuse — including by an employer or a member of the household.
navh.hours: 24 hours. If the danger is happening now, call 999 first.

scamShield.name: ScamShield Helpline
scamShield.hint: Unsure whether a job offer, loan, agent fee or money request is a scam? Check before you pay anything.

policeHotline.name: Police Hotline (non-urgent)
policeHotline.hint: Give information or follow up on a case when nobody is in immediate danger.
policeHotline.hours: If you are in danger right now, call 999 instead.

prepare.location: Say where you are first — block and unit number, road name, or the nearest MRT station or landmark. Help can be sent while you explain the rest.
prepare.what: Then say what happened and whether anyone is hurt or bleeding.
prepare.identity: Have your name, work permit or FIN number, and your employer's or dormitory's name ready.
prepare.interpreter: Ask for an interpreter if English is difficult. 999, 995 and the worker helplines can find someone who speaks your language.
prepare.stay: Stay on the line until the operator tells you it is fine to hang up.
prepare.airtime: 1800 numbers are free from a landline, but your mobile plan may still charge airtime.
prepare.save: Save these numbers in your phone today. In an emergency you may have no data left to open this page.

accountsGuide.title: Essential Accounts Guide
accountsGuide.subtitle: How to open the accounts that keep your salary safe, let you send money, and unlock government services — with official links and maps.
accountsGuide.bnplNote: This guide does not cover "Buy Now Pay Later" apps (e.g. Atome, Grab PayLater). They involve no credit check and real late fees that can snowball into debt — avoid them, especially if you are still repaying recruitment fees.
accountsGuide.safetyNote: Never share your bank PIN, OTP, Singpass password or PayNow QR with an agent, employer or stranger. No real bank or government officer will ask you to transfer money to "unlock" your account.
accountsGuide.disclaimer: General information only — always confirm current steps on the official website, and ask your employer or the bank directly if unsure. Partner links below may earn this app a small referral fee; the worker-facing tools stay free.
accountsGuide.pagePartnersSubtitle: Optional links from partners who help keep this guide free. Only open ones you trust.
accountsGuide.sponsoredNote: Sponsored — helps keep this free app running for workers.
accountsGuide.mapsTitle: Maps — find a bank branch or MOM
accountsGuide.mapsSubtitle: Tap to open Google Maps near you.

bank.name: Bank Account
bank.why: If you live in a dormitory, MOM requires your salary to be paid electronically into your own bank account — not cash to your employer or agent. A bank account also lets you save and remit through licensed channels (needed for Myanmar's remittance rule).
bank.how: Bring your passport and Work Permit/S Pass card to a bank. Some employers help Work Permit holders open a POSB account — ask first.

steps.docs: Bring passport + Work Permit / S Pass / EP card (originals). Some banks also ask for your employer's letter or address proof.
steps.employer: Ask your employer whether they already open POSB/DBS accounts for Work Permit staff through MOM WP Online. That can be faster than walking in alone.
steps.branch: Or walk into POSB, DBS, OCBC or UOB. Ask for a basic savings account for a work-pass holder. Keep your own ATM card and PIN — do not hand them over.
steps.keepBook: If your employer keeps the bank book, you still have the right to check it regularly and confirm salary hits every month.

links.posb: POSB — open or manage an account

paynow.name: PayNow
paynow.tagline: Instant transfers with your mobile number
paynow.why: PayNow lets you send and receive money instantly between Singapore banks for free using a mobile number — used for splitting bills, paying small shops, and topping up e-wallets.
paynow.how: Set it up inside your bank app after the account is open.

steps.openApp: Open your bank's mobile app (POSB digibank, DBS, OCBC, UOB, etc.).
steps.linkNumber: Find PayNow / Proxy settings and link your Singapore mobile number (and optionally NRIC/FIN) to your bank account.
steps.testSend: Send yourself S$0.01 (or a tiny amount) from another account, or ask a friend, to confirm the link works before you rely on it.

links.absPayNow: ABS: what PayNow is and how it works

singpass.name: Singpass
singpass.why: Singpass is how you log into government e-services — Work Permit status, MOM forms, and other official portals. Work-pass holders with a FIN can register.
singpass.how: Register online about 1–3 working days after your pass is issued, using face verification.

steps.waitPass: Wait until your Work Permit / S Pass / EP is issued and you have a FIN printed on the card.
steps.register: Go to the Singpass website or app and choose Register. Enter your FIN and details exactly as on the card.
steps.faceVerify: Complete face verification with a live selfie. Use a Singapore mobile number for OTP where asked.
steps.app: Install the Singpass app, set a passcode, and turn on biometric login if your phone supports it.

grabpay.name: GrabPay Wallet (top-up only)
grabpay.why: A prepaid e-wallet for transport and food. This is different from GrabPay PayLater (credit). Only use the top-up wallet.
grabpay.how: Download Grab, register, and top up with PayNow or bank transfer — never borrow through PayLater.

steps.download: Install Grab from the App Store or Google Play and register with your Singapore mobile number.
steps.topUp: Open GrabPay Wallet and top up using PayNow, bank transfer, or cash options shown in the app.
steps.avoidPayLater: Ignore GrabPay PayLater / PayLater offers. They are credit products with late fees — not needed for a prepaid wallet.

restDay.title: Rest Day Rights
restDay.subtitle: Domestic workers and Work Permit holders are covered by different laws. Pick the section that matches your pass, then confirm on MOM's own pages before you act.

jump.mdwHint: Weekly rest day under MOM's Work Permit conditions, including the 2023 mandatory day.
jump.wp: I hold a Work Permit or S Pass (not a maid)
jump.wpHint: Weekly rest day under the Employment Act — construction, factory, shipyard, services.

mdw.title: Domestic workers
mdw.subtitle: Migrant domestic workers are not covered by the Employment Act. Rest days are a Work Permit condition under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act.

facts.weekly: You are entitled to one rest day every week. You and your employer must agree which day it is — it does not have to be a Sunday.
facts.agreeDay: Your employer cannot make you work on a rest day unless you agree. Agreement should be mutual, not a threat of repatriation or withheld salary.
facts.mandatoryOne: Since 1 January 2023, at least one rest day each month must be a real day off. Neither you nor your employer can trade that one day for money.
facts.compensation: For the other weekly rest days, if you agree to work, your employer must pay at least one extra day's salary on top of your monthly pay — or give you a replacement rest day in the same month.
facts.written: Write the arrangement down (which day, which days you work instead, how much extra pay). MOM's rest-day guide includes a sample agreement.
facts.enforcement: Employers who refuse the mandatory rest day can be warned, barred from hiring domestic workers, and prosecuted under the Employment of Foreign Manpower Act (fine up to S$10,000, or jail, or both).

mdw.flexTitle: How the rest day can be taken
mdw.flexSubtitle: These flexibilities need both of you to agree. They do not cancel the mandatory day.

flex.anyDay: It can be any day of the week, not only Sunday.
flex.halfDays: It can be one full day, or two half-days.
flex.stayHome: You may spend it at home. Staying in the house does not mean you have to work — a rest day is a day off work.
flex.defer: If you cannot take it this month, it can be deferred by up to one calendar month. You must then take it by the end of the next month.

mdw.payTitle: How extra rest-day pay is calculated
mdw.paySubtitle: MOM's formula: monthly salary divided by 26, no matter how many days are in that month. The extra is paid on top of your usual salary.
mdw.payExample: MOM's example: monthly salary S${salary} ÷ {divisor} = S${dayRate} per rest day worked. Two rest days worked = S${salary} + S$50.
mdw.payLink: MOM: how to calculate pay in lieu of a rest day

wp.title: Work Permit and S Pass holders (not domestic workers)
wp.subtitle: If you are covered by Part 4 of the Employment Act (most workmen earning up to S$4,500 a month, and most other employees earning up to S$2,600), these rest-day rules apply.

facts.weekly: Your employer must give you one rest day every week. A rest day is unpaid — it is a day you do not work.
facts.wholeDay: A rest day is one whole day, midnight to midnight. For shift workers it can be a continuous 30 hours.
facts.maxGap: The longest gap allowed between two rest days is 12 days.
facts.roster: If your rest day is not a Sunday, your employer should give you a monthly roster before the month starts.
facts.cannotCompel: Your employer cannot force you to work on a rest day except in exceptional circumstances.
facts.employerPay: If your employer asks you to work that day: up to half your normal hours = 1 day's pay; more than half = 2 days' pay; beyond normal hours = 2 days' pay plus overtime.
facts.noTimeOff: If your employer asked you to work, they cannot give you a day off later instead of this extra pay.

denied.subtitle: The call is confidential. MOM will not tell your employer who reported them if you ask to stay anonymous to the other party.

steps.call: Call the helpline that matches your pass — MOM's domestic-worker line, or MWC / CDE if you are not sure.
steps.report: Or report the infringement online. You must give MOM your identity so they can follow up, but they can keep it from your employer.
steps.centre: You can also go in person to MOM Services Centre, Hall A, 1500 Bendemeer Road.
steps.salary: If the problem is unpaid rest-day compensation, TADM handles salary claims — raise it while you are still in Singapore.

offDayGuide.title: Off-Day Guide
offDayGuide.subtitle: Real places in Singapore where migrant communities gather, shop and connect on rest days.

peninsulaPlaza.name: Peninsula Plaza ("Little Myanmar")
peninsulaPlaza.description: A shopping centre known as Singapore's Myanmar hub since the 1990s — Myanmar restaurants, grocery stores, travel agencies, and money changers, especially busy on Sundays.
peninsulaPlaza.food: Myanmar restaurants on the upper floors — mohinga, tea-leaf salad, curry and rice at prices close to home cooking.
peninsulaPlaza.gettingThere: City Hall MRT (NS25 / EW13), take Exit B and walk about 5 minutes. Busiest on Sunday afternoons.

burmeseTemple.name: Burmese Buddhist Temple
burmeseTemple.description: Singapore's only traditional Burmese-style Buddhist temple, founded in 1875 — a spiritual and cultural gathering point for the community.
burmeseTemple.food: No restaurant inside. Bring water; there are shops on Balestier Road, about 10 minutes' walk.
burmeseTemple.gettingThere: Toa Payoh MRT (NS19), then bus, or Novena MRT (NS20) and about 15 minutes' walk.

farrerPark.name: Farrer Park / Stamford Road area
farrerPark.description: An informal Sunday gathering spot near Little India where many Myanmar workers meet friends on their day off.
farrerPark.food: Every kind of South and Southeast Asian food in the surrounding streets, much of it under $6.
farrerPark.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8). The crowd builds through Sunday afternoon and into the evening.

tekkaCentre.name: Tekka Centre, Little India
tekkaCentre.description: A wet market and hawker centre at the exit of Little India MRT, and the centre of Sunday life for South Asian workers — cheap food, money transfer shops, phone top-ups and the crowds along Serangoon Road. Open daily 6.30am–9pm.
tekkaCentre.food: Hawker centre downstairs — biryani, roti prata, fish head curry. Among the cheapest hot meals in the city.
tekkaCentre.gettingThere: Little India MRT (NE7 / DT12), the exit opens almost onto it. Open daily 6.30am–9pm.

bangladeshSquare.name: "Bangladesh Square", Desker Road
bangladeshSquare.description: The junction of Desker Road and Lembu Road, long known as the main Sunday meeting point for Bangladeshi workers. Busiest on Sunday evenings, with food stalls and Bengali groceries in the surrounding streets.
bangladeshSquare.food: Bengali restaurants and grocery shops through the surrounding streets, busiest on Sunday evening.
bangladeshSquare.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8), then walk. Desker Road meets Lembu Road.

mustafa.name: Mustafa Centre
mustafa.description: A 24-hour department store near Farrer Park MRT, used for everything from groceries and phone cards to gold and remittance. Open at any hour, which matters if your rest day starts late.
mustafa.food: Food court inside, and the surrounding streets are full of cheap South Asian restaurants.
mustafa.gettingThere: Farrer Park MRT (NE8), about 3 minutes' walk. Open 24 hours.

peoplesPark.name: People's Park Complex, Chinatown
peoplesPark.description: A mall beside Chinatown MRT that is the main gathering point for workers from mainland China — regional Chinese food, money changers, remittance counters and travel agencies under one roof.
peoplesPark.food: Regional Chinese food court — Sichuan, Northeastern, Hunan — plus a hawker centre next door.
peoplesPark.gettingThere: Chinatown MRT (NE4 / DT19), the mall is right beside the station exit.

gardensByTheBay.name: Gardens by the Bay
gardensByTheBay.description: The Supertrees and the outdoor gardens are free to walk through, and the light show at the Supertree Grove runs free in the evening. The two glass domes (Flower Dome, Cloud Forest), the Skyway bridge and the Supertree Observatory all charge admission — you can have a full afternoon without paying for any of them.
gardensByTheBay.food: Hawker-priced food at Satay by the Bay, at the far end of the gardens. The cafes near the domes are tourist-priced.
gardensByTheBay.gettingThere: Bayfront MRT (CE1 / DT16), Exit B, then follow the underground link. About 10 minutes' walk to the Supertrees.

botanicGardens.name: Singapore Botanic Gardens
botanicGardens.description: A UNESCO World Heritage site, free to enter every day for everyone. Lawns, lakes, a rainforest trail and shade — the easiest place in Singapore to spend a whole day without spending money. Only the National Orchid Garden inside charges admission.
botanicGardens.food: Food court near the Tanglin Gate at ordinary prices; the restaurants inside are expensive. Bringing your own food is allowed and common.
botanicGardens.gettingThere: Botanic Gardens MRT (CC19 / DT9) opens directly onto the Bukit Timah Gate.

marinaBarrage.name: Marina Barrage
marinaBarrage.description: A dam with a grass roof, open 24 hours and free. The roof is one of the best places in Singapore to sit with a view of the whole skyline — people fly kites, picnic and stay till late. Popular with worker groups on Sundays.
marinaBarrage.food: Nothing much on site beyond a small shop. Most people bring food; there is a hawker centre at Marina South Pier or Satay by the Bay nearby.
marinaBarrage.gettingThere: No station at the door. Bayfront MRT (CE1 / DT16) then about 20 minutes' walk through Gardens by the Bay, or bus 400.

jewelChangi.name: Jewel Changi Airport
jewelChangi.description: The indoor waterfall — the Rain Vortex — is free to see, and free to sit and watch. In the evening it becomes a light and music show. You do not need a flight or a ticket to go in. The Canopy Park playgrounds and walkways upstairs are the part that charges.
jewelChangi.food: A very large food court in the basement at normal Singapore prices, plus every fast food chain.
jewelChangi.gettingThere: Changi Airport MRT (CG2), then follow signs — Jewel connects directly to Terminal 1. Rain Vortex runs 10am–10pm.

sentosa.name: Sentosa Island
sentosa.description:
A whole island that can cost you nothing, or a lot, depending entirely on how you go. Walking in across the Boardwalk from VivoCity is free — Sentosa's own site lists the admission charge for walking in as FREE. Once you are on the island, the Sentosa Express monorail, the island buses and the beach shuttle are all free to use, and the three beaches (Siloso, Palawan, Tanjong) cost nothing. So a full day of beach, sea and walking is genuinely free.

The paid part is the attractions. Universal Studios starts around $76, the Oceanarium around $43, Adventure Cove around $29, Wings of Time around $22. None of them is needed for a good day out.

Note: there is no Disneyland in Singapore — the theme park here is Universal Studios, on this island.
sentosa.food: Expensive at the resort side. Cheaper: eat at VivoCity's basement food court before you cross, or bring your own — the beaches allow picnics.
sentosa.gettingThere: HarbourFront MRT (NE1 / CC29), then VivoCity Lobby F on Level 1, and walk across the Boardwalk. Free, about 15 minutes. Part of the Boardwalk is closed for construction until around 2030 and walkers are redirected through a covered linkway — the route is still open, just signposted differently. The Sentosa Express from VivoCity costs $4 one way if you prefer to ride in.

offDayGuide.sourceDisclaimer: Locations are widely documented community gathering spots, not official recommendations. Please travel safely and let someone know your plans on your day off.
offDayGuide.noPlacesYet: We don't have {country} community places listed yet. Many Malaysians here live across the island rather than gathering in one area, so there is no single hub to point to — if you know one worth adding, tell us.
offDayGuide.museumWarningTitle: Museums are not free for work pass holders
offDayGuide.museumWarningBody: National Heritage Board museums — the National Museum, Asian Civilisations Museum and others — are free only for Singapore citizens and PRs. On a Work Permit, S Pass or Employment Pass you pay the full price (around $10 for an adult, $5 with a student or senior card). Worth knowing before you travel across the island expecting free entry.
offDayGuide.libraryNote: Public libraries are free to walk into, sit in air-conditioning and read all day — no membership needed for that. You only need a membership to borrow books home, and foreigners pay a yearly fee for it; check the current amount on NLB's site.

rates.checkIntro: Rates move during the day and every provider sets its own, so confirm the exact rate in the provider's own app before you send. What you can check here is more important: whether the company is licensed by MAS at all. If it is not on this list and your money goes missing, there is no regulator to complain to.
rates.providersNote: We are not affiliated with any provider and receive nothing if you use them.
rates.compareFee: Compare the total cost, not just the rate — a good rate with a high fee can be worse overall.
rates.compareLicence: Use a provider licensed by MAS. Unlicensed transfer means no recourse if the money disappears.
rates.panelDisclaimer: Indicative only. Rates for India, China, Bangladesh and Malaysia are the international mid-market rate — your provider's rate after fees will be lower. Myanmar's is from an independent rate-tracking site rather than a bank, since no bank or e-wallet here publishes a comparable daily figure — treat it as a rough indication only. Always confirm the exact rate in your provider's own app before you send.
rates.compareOfficial: Myanmar requires a share of overseas wages to be remitted through official channels. Keep your transfer receipts.
rates.topWarning: Rates change during the day. Always confirm the final rate and fees in the provider’s own app or shop before you send money.
rates.myanmarOfficialAlert: Myanmar rules may require a share of overseas wages to be remitted through official channels. Keep every receipt. Unofficial agents who promise “better rates” can take your money with no MAS protection.
rates.safeSendIntro: Use this checklist every time you remit, especially to Myanmar.

safeSend.compareTotal: Compare total cost (rate + fee + receiving fee), not the headline rate alone.
safeSend.checkLicence: Confirm the company appears on the MAS financial institutions / payment service providers lists linked below.
safeSend.confirmRate: Check today’s rate in the provider’s app or at the counter — our panel is indicative only.
safeSend.keepReceipt: Save the transfer receipt and reference number until the money arrives.
safeSend.avoidAgent: Do not hand cash to a stranger or “agent” who is not a licensed shop or app — if it disappears, you may have no recourse.

rates.channelsIntro: Pick a channel that fits your amount, speed and risk tolerance. Licensed channels first.

channels.bank: Bank transfer / telegraphic transfer — slower, often safer; ask your bank about fees to Myanmar or your home country.
channels.licensed: MAS-licensed remittance companies and e-wallets — common for workers; always verify the licence list.
channels.shop: Money changers / remittance counters in places like Peninsula Plaza or Little India — check the rate board and ask for a receipt.
channels.app: Licensed remittance apps — convenient, but confirm fees and receiving bank/e-wallet support in Myanmar before you lock the rate.

mistakes.mistakeUnlicensed: Sending through an unlicensed person — no MAS complaint path if funds vanish.
mistakes.mistakeCashStranger: Giving cash to a friend-of-a-friend “agent” with only a WhatsApp promise.
mistakes.mistakeIgnoreFee: Chasing the best rate while ignoring a large fixed fee.
mistakes.mistakeNoReceipt: Leaving without a receipt or screenshot of the transaction reference.
mistakes.mistakeFakeRate: Trusting a screenshot from a chat group instead of the provider’s live quote.

transport.title: Bus & MRT — how to travel in Singapore
transport.subtitle: Map links, route planning tools, and the fare rules that decide whether your trip is charged once or multiple times.

quickStart.openPlanner: Open the LTA journey planner (or MyTransport app), enter where you are and where you are going, then follow one route all the way the first few times.
quickStart.checkLastTrain: If you travel at night, check the last train for your exact station and direction before you leave. There is no single network-wide last-train time.
quickStart.choosePayment: Choose one payment method and stick to it for that trip. Do not switch cards halfway.
quickStart.saveStops: For buses, save your boarding stop and your alighting stop in the app so you do not miss your stop.
quickStart.leaveBuffer: Leave 10-15 extra minutes when going to appointments (MOM, hospital, embassy).

transport.payIntro: No paper ticket needed. Tap a card or phone on entry and on exit.

pay.payCard: SimplyGo EZ-Link card — buy and top up at MRT station ticketing machines and convenience stores.
pay.payBank: A contactless bank card or mobile wallet (Visa, Mastercard, AMEX, NETS Tap) — tap directly, no separate transit card needed.
pay.payBalance: Keep enough value in your transit card. If balance is too low, the reader can reject it and you may be denied boarding.

transport.payNoDisplay: SimplyGo cards do not show your fare or remaining balance at the gate. Check both in the SimplyGo app.
transport.payAxs: From 29 August 2026 you can no longer top up EZ-Link or SimplyGo cards at AXS machines. Use station machines, the app, or a convenience store.
transport.tapTitle: 2. Tap in and tap out — both times

tap.tapIn: Tap when you board the bus or enter the MRT gate.
tap.tapOut: Tap again when you get off the bus or leave the MRT gate.
tap.busDoor: On buses, board from the front door and exit from the rear door unless the bus signs say otherwise.

transport.tapWarning: If you forget to tap out, you are charged the maximum fare for that line. This is the most common and most expensive mistake.
transport.fareDistance: Fares are based on the total distance of your whole journey, not the number of vehicles you take.
transport.fareTransfer: Changing between bus and train inside one journey does not start a new fare. You are charged once for the distance.
transport.transferIntro: Several trips count as one journey only if all of these are true:

transfer.transferTime: No more than 2 hours between your first boarding and your last boarding in the journey.
transfer.transferSameBus: You do not board the same bus service number twice in a row.
transfer.transferStations: At Bukit Panjang, Newton and Tampines you must tap out of one line and tap in to the next. Do this within 15 minutes or it becomes a new journey with a new fare.

transport.nightIntro: Trains generally run from around 5.30am to around midnight, but station-by-station times differ.

night.night1: Check first and last train timings on SMRT or SBS Transit pages for your station and direction.
night.night2: If you miss the last train, use bus directions in MyTransport/Google Maps before booking an expensive ride.
night.night3: When phone battery is low at night, screenshot your route before leaving.

maps.smrt: SMRT train service updates and timings
maps.sbst: SBS Transit train service updates and timings

transport.mapsTip: For a bus, the planner tells you the stop name and how many stops to stay on. Bus stops show the service numbers that stop there and a stop ID you can check in the app.
transport.hubsTitle: Quick map links for common worker destinations

mistakes.mistake1: Forgetting to tap out — you pay the maximum fare.
mistakes.mistake2: Using one card to enter and a different card to exit — charged as separate trips.
mistakes.mistake3: Taking a long break mid-journey — after 2 hours it becomes a new journey and you pay again.
mistakes.mistake4: Boarding the same bus number twice in a row — the second ride is charged as a new journey.
mistakes.mistake5: Using outdated blog screenshots for routes — always check live planner links before leaving.

drivingLicense.title: Driving licence guide
drivingLicense.subtitle: Convert a foreign licence, prepare for BTT/FTT, train at authorised centres, find maps and official documents — plus free Myanmar community helpers.
drivingLicense.topWarning: Rules and fees change. Always confirm on the Traffic Police and LTA pages linked below before you pay or book.
drivingLicense.overviewTitle: 1. Can you drive on a foreign licence?

overview.shortStay: If you stay under about 12 months, you may drive on a valid foreign licence (plus an International Driving Permit or official English translation if the licence is not in English).
overview.longStay: If your pass is for 12 months or more (most Work Permits, S Pass, EP), Traffic Police expect you to convert to a Singapore licence — do not keep driving on the foreign one past the allowed period.
overview.asean: ASEAN-issued licences often do not need an IDP for short stays, but conversion still applies for long-term pass holders. Check the official Traffic Police page for your case.
overview.eligibility: Conversion usually requires age 18+, a valid unexpired foreign licence, and passing the Basic Theory Test (BTT) in Singapore.

drivingLicense.convertTitle: 2. Convert a foreign licence (most pass holders)
drivingLicense.convertIntro: Typical path after you already hold a licence from your home country:

convertSteps.passBtt: Enrol at one of the three authorised driving centres and pass the Basic Theory Test (BTT).
convertSteps.gatherDocs: Prepare passport, work/long-term pass, foreign licence, photo, and any translation or residency proof Traffic Police asks for.
convertSteps.preAssessment: Complete the Foreign Licence Pre-assessment on the Traffic Police e-service. Eligible applicants receive a link to book.
convertSteps.appointment: Book and attend your appointment at Traffic Police Headquarters (10 Ubi Avenue 3). Bring originals — incomplete files are rejected.
convertSteps.payCollect: Pay the conversion fee (about S$50; confirm current amount on the official page). Keep the receipt; your Singapore licence is usually posted after approval.

drivingLicense.convertWpNote: Work Permit and S Pass holders who convert often receive a Class 3C licence for standard cars. Exact class depends on Traffic Police rules and your foreign licence — confirm at submission.
drivingLicense.docsIntro: Traffic Police may ask for more. Bring originals and photocopies where possible.

docs.passportPass: Passport and current work / long-term pass (and FIN card if you have one).
docs.foreignLicence: Valid foreign driving licence (not expired, suspended, or cancelled).
docs.translation: If the licence is not in English: International Driving Permit or official English translation from an authorised translator / embassy.
docs.photo: Recent passport-size photo (matte/semi-matte, white background, usually within 3 months).
docs.residencyProof: If you got the foreign licence after your first Singapore pass or PR: proof of about 6 months’ stay in the country that issued the licence.
docs.wpHistory: Work Permit holders may need MOM employment history printouts — follow the Traffic Police checklist.

drivingLicense.learnerIntro: If you never held a licence, you train at an authorised centre. Exact packages differ by centre.

learner.enrolCentre: Enrol at BBDC, CDC, or SSDC and pass eyesight / medical checks as required.
learner.bttPdl: Pass BTT, then apply for a Provisional Driving Licence (PDL) via Traffic Police before on-road lessons.
learner.lessonsFtt: Complete practical lessons and pass the Final Theory Test (FTT) when required for your class.
learner.practical: Pass the practical driving test for your class (e.g. Class 3 / 3A car, or Class 2B motorcycle).
learner.qdl: Apply for your Qualified Driving Licence (QDL) after you pass — fees and postal delivery follow Traffic Police instructions.

drivingLicense.centresSubtitle: Open in Google Maps. Book tests on each centre’s website, not only by walking in.

centres.ssdc: Singapore Safety Driving Centre (SSDC), Ang Mo Kio
centres.tpHq: Traffic Police HQ — 10 Ubi Avenue 3 (conversion appointments)

drivingLicense.vocationalIntro: A normal Class 3 licence is not enough to drive for hire. Vocational licences are separate and have strict eligibility.
drivingLicense.vocationalAlert: New Private Hire (PDVL) and Taxi (TDVL) licences are for Singapore citizens only (age and experience rules also apply). Most Work Permit / S Pass / EP holders cannot apply for a new PDVL to drive Grab or similar.

vocational.pdvlCitizenOnly: PDVL (private hire / chauffeured car): Singapore citizen, typically age 30+, valid Class 3/3A for more than 1 year — confirm on LTA OneMotoring / GoBusiness.
vocational.tdvlCitizenOnly: TDVL (taxi): also restricted to Singapore citizens with LTA training and checks.
vocational.odvlBus: Some bus vocational paths (e.g. omnibus) may allow Work Permit holders whose vocation is bus driver — only if your employer and LTA allow it. Never assume; check OneMotoring.
vocational.checkOfficial: Before paying any “agent” who promises a Grab licence for foreigners, read the official LTA / GoBusiness pages linked below.

mistakes.mistakeDriveExpired: Driving on a foreign licence after you should have converted — fines and insurance problems.
mistakes.mistakeSkipBtt: Going to Traffic Police without a passed BTT — you will be turned away.
mistakes.mistakeNoTranslation: Bringing a non-English licence without IDP or certified translation.
mistakes.mistakePdvlHope: Paying someone who claims Work Permit holders can get a new Grab/PDVL licence — that is usually false.
mistakes.mistakeOutdatedBlog: Following old blog fees or steps — always re-check official pages on the day you apply.
mistakes.mistakePayAgent: Paying a middleman who promises to “skip” BTT or TP appointment — you still must follow official steps.
mistakes.mistakeDemerit: Ignoring demerit letters or driving without a P-plate in probation — easy way to lose a new licence.

drivingLicense.disclaimer: This page is general guidance only. Traffic Police and LTA set the real rules, fees, and eligibility. Confirm every step on their websites before you spend money or take leave from work.
drivingLicense.testsIntro: These are the main Traffic Police tests you will hear about. Exact fees change — check your centre and the official pages.

tests.btt: Basic Theory Test (BTT) — traffic rules and signs. Required for foreign-licence conversion and before a Provisional Driving Licence (PDL).
tests.ftt: Final Theory Test (FTT) — deeper rules for learners before the practical test (class-dependent).
tests.rtt: Riding Theory Test (RTT) — for motorcycle classes (e.g. Class 2B) instead of / in addition to car theory paths.
tests.practical: Practical driving / riding test — on-road assessment after lessons and theory. Pass before you get a Qualified Driving Licence (QDL).
tests.booking: Book tests through your driving centre’s website or counter. Bring FIN/pass and follow their photo / eye-check rules.

drivingLicense.classesIntro: Class names appear on your Singapore licence. Confirm what your foreign licence maps to at conversion.

classes.class3: Class 3 — manual cars (and usually autos) under the older full Class 3 rules for eligible pass types.
classes.class3a: Class 3A — automatic cars only (common for many EP/DP conversions when the foreign licence was automatic).
classes.class3c: Class 3C — often issued to Work Permit / S Pass holders on conversion for standard motorcars; confirm with Traffic Police.
classes.class2b: Class 2B — motorcycles up to 200cc (separate enrolment, RTT and practical bike test).

drivingLicense.trainingTitle: 8. Training tips (before you pay a big package)
drivingLicense.trainingIntro: Authorised centres sell theory + practical packages. Compare carefully.

training.chooseCentre: Compare BBDC, CDC and SSDC for location, language support, and package price — not only the cheapest online ad.
training.theoryPractice: Use centre e-trial / practice papers for BTT (and FTT/RTT if needed). Passing BTT does not by itself finish conversion.
training.practicalHours: Ask how many practical hours are included, cancellation fees, and whether an instructor who speaks your language is available.
training.feesVary: Expect separate line items: enrolment, theory tests, PDL, practical lessons, practical test, QDL fee. Totals differ by centre and class.

drivingLicense.passMarksIntro: Know the score you need before you book a test. Centres follow Traffic Police standards.

passMarks.theoryScore: BTT and FTT: pass mark is usually 90% — at least 45 correct out of 50 questions.
passMarks.theoryFormat: Typical theory format: 50 multiple-choice questions in about 45 minutes (confirm on your booking slip).
passMarks.practicalDemerit: Practical driving test: examiners award demerit points for mistakes. Too many demerit points = fail (centres often cite a fail around 20 demerit points — confirm with your instructor).
passMarks.fttWindow: After you pass FTT, you usually must pass the practical car test within 2 years, or you retake FTT.
passMarks.rttWindow: After you pass RTT (motorcycle), you usually must pass the practical riding test within 1 year, or you retake RTT.

drivingLicense.passMarksNote: Conversion applicants who only need BTT still follow the same BTT pass mark. Always re-check your centre’s current rules on test day.
drivingLicense.demeritIntro: Singapore uses the Driver Improvement Points System (DIPS). Points add up for traffic offences and can suspend or revoke your licence.

demerit.whatIsDips: Each scheduled offence adds demerit points. Stay offence-free long enough and points can be cleared under Traffic Police rules.
demerit.probationYear: New Class 2B / 3 / 3A / 3C / 3CA drivers are usually on probation for 1 year from the date the licence is granted.
demerit.pPlate: During probation you must display the Probation (P) plate front and rear. Missing plates can mean a fine; repeat offences in probation can revoke the licence.
demerit.probationLimit: Probation drivers (current rule): about 13 or more demerit points in the 1-year probation → licence can be revoked. You may need to wait 1 year before retaking all tests.
demerit.fullLicenceLimit: Non-probation drivers with no prior suspension (current rule): about 24 or more demerit points within 24 months → liable for suspension (first suspension often about 12 weeks).
demerit.change2027: From 1 Jan 2027, Traffic Police plans stricter thresholds (reports: ~18 points in 24 months for non-probation; ~12 for probation). Confirm nearer the date on official pages.
demerit.afterRevoke: Check your points anytime via SPF “Check Driver Improvement Points” (Singpass). After revocation you must retake required theory and practical tests.

drivingLicense.demeritWarning: Demerit thresholds and suspension lengths change. Treat numbers here as a study guide — verify on SPF / BTT handbook before you drive.
drivingLicense.finesIntro: Examples of demerit points and typical composition fines for light vehicles. Heavy vehicles often cost more. Court cases can be higher.

fines.seatbelt: Not wearing a seatbelt — often about 3–4 demerit points and around S$150 composition fine (confirm current schedule).
fines.speedLow: Speeding about 1–20 km/h over limit — often about 4 demerit points and around S$150.
fines.speedMid: Speeding about 21–30 km/h over — often about 6 demerit points and a higher fine (commonly cited around S$200+).
fines.redLight: Beating a red light — often about 12 demerit points and a substantial fine (commonly cited around S$200–S$400+). Alone this can revoke a probation licence.
fines.phone: Using a handheld phone while driving — often about 12 demerit points plus fine. Hands-free rules still apply — check the current law.
fines.signal: Failing to signal / some signalling offences — lower demerit or fine-only in some schedules; still ticketed.
fines.noteAmounts: Exact demerit + fine pairs are in the official DIPS schedule inside the Basic Theory handbook. Do not rely on WhatsApp screenshots.

drivingLicense.finesDisclaimer: Fines and points are set by Traffic Police and can change. This list is for awareness only — not legal advice and not a full offence schedule.
